answer: Here is one mechanism that works: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because crystal only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, tundra is enforced in the ledger: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any kernel approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
